review_notes: I read the whole file and checked its coordinate and Hilbert-space helper definitions against Mathlib's PiL2 and PiLp files. I also looked at the repo's other definitions of `l2Vec3Equiv`, `l2BasisVec3` and `basisVec`, and at the weak-test-function structure. Two findings came out of this: `l2Vec3Equiv` and `l2BasisVec`. I did not flag the Schwartz-map encodings, since they are built from Mathlib's `toSchwartzMap`, `compCLMOfContinuousLinearEquiv` and `postcompCLM`. I also did not flag `gradientOfCovector`, because I found no exact Mathlib counterpart for a complex-valued covector. `fourier_postcompCLM` is a theorem, so it is outside this rubric. Remaining uncertainty: I did not confirm that every use site elaborates against the `EuclideanSpace` spelling. The definitions agree by `rfl`-level unfolding of `abbrev`s, but that is a reading of the sources, not a compile check. Both findings need the same caveat. `L2Vec3` is the abbrev `PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ)`, so it is defeq to `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`, but it is not written that way.

findings.problem: This is exactly Mathlib's `EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin 3) ℝ`. `L2Vec3` is `PiLp 2 (fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ)`, which is `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3)`. `EuclideanSpace` is an abbrev, and `EuclideanSpace.equiv` is an abbrev for `PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 𝕜 _`. The file's definition is therefore the same term with the arguments filled in, and it is a duplicate concept. The repo also defines a second `CKN.l2Vec3Equiv` with the same body in `JSpaceFourierPotentialBase.lean`, so it has now been written twice.
findings.proposed_change: Delete the local `def`. Use `EuclideanSpace.equiv (Fin 3) ℝ` directly. If a short name is wanted, make it an `abbrev` or notation for that, and keep one copy (also replacing the duplicate in `JSpaceFourierPotentialBase.lean`). The `l2Vec3Equiv` call sites in this file should continue to typecheck, because the two terms are defeq.
findings.benefit: There is no private parallel definition to keep in sync. Readers see at once that this is the standard coordinate equivalence on Euclidean space. The two copies of `l2Vec3Equiv` in the repo are merged, and Mathlib's existing lemmas about `EuclideanSpace.equiv` become directly usable.

evidence.excerpt:
abbrev EuclideanSpace.equiv : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 ι ≃L[𝕜] ι → 𝕜 :=
  PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 𝕜 _

def l2Vec3Equiv : L2Vec3 ≃L[ℝ] Vec3 :=
  PiLp.continuousLinearEquiv 2 ℝ (fun _ : Fin 3 => ℝ)

findings.problem: `l2BasisVec i` is `toLp 2 (Pi.single i 1)` on `PiLp 2 (fun _ => ℝ)`. `CKN.basisVec i` unfolds to `Pi.single i 1`. This is Mathlib's `EuclideanSpace.single i 1`, which is an abbrev for `PiLp.single 2 i 1 := toLp p (Pi.single i a)`. It is also the standard orthonormal basis `EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 3) ℝ i`. Mathlib already has `PiLp.norm_single`, `EuclideanSpace.single_apply`, `EuclideanSpace.inner_single_right` and `EuclideanSpace.basisFun_apply`. The file re-proves the norm fact in `l2BasisVec_norm` and the inner-product fact in `inner_l2BasisVec` by unfolding `simp`. The repo also has a second copy under the name `l2BasisVec3` in `JSpaceFourierPotentialBase.lean`.
findings.proposed_change: Remove `l2BasisVec`. Use `EuclideanSpace.single i (1 : ℝ)` (or `EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin 3) ℝ i`) in `gradientOfCovectorLinear` and throughout. Replace `l2BasisVec_norm` by `PiLp.norm_single` followed by `norm_one`. Replace `inner_l2BasisVec` by `EuclideanSpace.inner_single_right` (it gives `1 * conj (ξ i)`, which simplifies with `simp`). Merge with `l2BasisVec3` in the other file.
findings.benefit: This removes a locally defined basis vector, which in turn removes a norm lemma and an inner-product lemma that Mathlib already supplies. It also gives the definition the standard name that readers and automation recognise, and avoids duplicates inside the repo.

evidence.excerpt: abbrev EuclideanSpace.single (i : ι) (a : 𝕜) : EuclideanSpace 𝕜 ι := PiLp.single 2 i a
def single (i : ι) (a : β i) : PiLp p β := toLp p (Pi.single i a)
lemma norm_single (i : ι) (b : β i) : ‖single p i b‖ = ‖b‖
